{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMdNDs8AAAABZr6lpg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnXy5zhDSSAA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnXy5", "number": 49, "title": "Unify all MMD glTF demos into one visual-first GitHub Pages interface", "body": "## Problem

The public [mmd-gltf GitHub Pages demo](https://takahirox.github.io/mmd-gltf/) presents **Gene Light PMX vs. glTF** at the root, while the interactive **BDEF/SDEF/QDEF, VPD/VMD, morph, IK/append and physics** demo lives on a separate `rig.html` page. Many features already have implementations and synthetic demos, but visitors cannot discover and try them in one coherent interface. Both pages also rely on large blocks of prose, repeated qualifiers/secondary labels, and lengthy control groups instead of a clear visual hierarchy.

**Deliver one user-facing demo page at `/mmd-gltf/` that lets visitors inspect all currently implemented features without navigating to a separate page. The 3D content should explain the demo first; controls and short labels should support it.**

This is a **UI/integration redesign**, not a request for new glTF extensions, shaders, solvers, physics behavior, assets, or unimplemented MMD capabilities.

## Desired experience

A possible information architecture (use the simplest effective design; not a mandate for a framework or exact styling):

- **Primary model/preset selection**: switch in place between **Gene Light comparison** and the existing **synthetic test rigs/presets** (BDEF, SDEF, QDEF; vertex/bone/group/mixed morphs; IK/append; rigid-body physics). A compact model selector or visually grouped preset picker is preferable to navigation between HTML pages and a single unwieldy flat menu.
- **Large, dominant viewport**: keep the models the focus. For Gene Light, retain the **side-by-side PMX / glTF comparison** with synchronized orbit/zoom and front/side/back views. For synthetic rigs, use a clear in-place viewer with the existing pose/motion/physics functionality; do **not** fabricate an equivalent direct-PMX reference where none exists.
- **Compact contextual controls**: show only controls relevant to the selected model and capability. Keep a common small set for material (MMD Toon/PBR), Outline on/off, and camera/view operations where supported. For rigs, surface VPD pose/apply/reset, VMD play/pause/seek/loop, independent morph weights, IK switches, physics enable/step/reset, and the existing export/local-file workflows in appropriate contexts. Do not hide important supported functions permanently just to make the page look clean.
- **Layout over explanatory prose**: short, meaningful labels; clear grouping; prominent playback/viewport; understandable disabled/unavailable states. Avoid verbose secondary labels, duplicate statuses, explanations repeated beside each control, and paragraphs describing things already obvious in the UI. Make behavior discoverable by interaction, not a textual instruction manual. Keep concise help for genuinely non-obvious workflows (such as explicit name binding or local file encoding).
- **Light-gray backgrounds** (current `#d0d0d0`) so dark outlines remain visible; coherent visual styling and legibility in both Gene comparison panes and the rig viewer.
- **Responsive layout**: preserve usable viewport dimensions and make controls practical on desktop and narrow/mobile layouts; avoid overwhelming small screens with a permanently expanded control matrix.

## Existing starting points

- [`examples/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/index.html), [`examples/main.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/main.ts): synchronized Gene Light PMX/glTF comparison, material/Outline/view controls, required asset provenance and rights links.
- [`examples/rig.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/rig.html), [`examples/rig.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/rig.ts): current synthetic rigs and control workflows, including VPD/VMD from samples/files/retained curves, skinning modes, morphs, IK, physics and applied-state export.
- [`examples/style.css`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/style.css): current site styling.
- [`vite.config.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/vite.config.ts): both public entries and separate **test-only conformance pages**.
- [`tests/browser/`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/tree/main/tests/browser): current interactive/browser test coverage and numerical rendering fixtures.

Reuse the existing rendering, loader, converter and playback integrations. Restructure the page code as needed to prevent duplicated renderer ownership/animation loops or stale listeners when switching presets; **do not introduce an unrelated UI framework, new abstraction layer, or new dependency without need**.

## Requirements and constraints

1. **One discoverable user-facing page:** the root GitHub Pages URL directly exposes both Gene Light and all presently supported synthetic rig functionality using **in-page selection**. The implementation must not send users to `rig.html` to access functionality. A backwards-compatible redirect or link from the old `rig.html` URL is fine; internal conformance/test pages may remain separate and are **not** subject to this design requirement.
2. **Preserve feature coverage:** selecting a rig must preserve existing BDEF/SDEF/QDEF paths; VPD application/reset and local files/encoding/binding; VMD bytes/GLB/glTF sources, playback and seeking, local-file/binding; vertex/bone/mixed/group morph controls; supported IK/append and physics workflows; Toon/PBR, Outline and applied GLB/glTF export. The Gene view retains its two-source comparison. Each operation must act on the currently selected asset/scene. Do not quietly discard an existing operation or claim unsupported features are implemented.
3. **Clear, minimal UI:** the opening viewport and model selector should make the purpose obvious without reading a long paragraph. Prefer composition, whitespace, short plain labels, controls and sensible grouping over big paragraphs and multiple badges/secondary explanatory strings. Avoid adding new secondary labels everywhere as a substitute for layout. Keep diagnostics concise and actionable on error; do not bury key error messages.
4. **Preserve accuracy and necessary disclosures:** the left Gene Light renderer is a secondary reference, not original MMD; exact MMD visual/physics fidelity is unverified and some solver/physics behaviors are bounded profiles. Communicate this **once, concisely**, and provide an unobtrusive accessible place for methodological details (e.g. a small “About/Details” disclosure or link to docs). Do not misleadingly imply identical shading or verified original-MMD fidelity. Keep **all necessary Gene Light creator attribution, CC BY 4.0 / additional usage guidance, source notices and links** accessible and intact; legal notices are not expendable UI clutter.
5. **Predictable interaction/lifecycle:** switching models/presets, materials and Outline, replacing motion, toggling physics and uploading files must not leave hidden scenes animating, stale callbacks, unmanaged GPU/Ammo resources, incorrect camera state, or mismatched displayed controls. Keep interactions keyboard-accessible, labels discoverable to assistive technology, and readable contrast. An unavailable control should have an understandable disabled state or not be shown in that context.
6. **No behavior/spec changes:** retain existing v0.1 materials/outline and current skin/morph/animation/solver/physics semantics, numerical thresholds, asset provenance/hash restrictions, default WebGL2 with optional native WebGPU, current build paths and independent test harnesses. Do not use this UI task as a reason to alter draft specifications or promise full MMD coverage.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] At **`/mmd-gltf/`**, visitors can select **Gene Light** or each supported synthetic rig/preset and use the relevant controls **without another page navigation**. Desktop and narrow/mobile layouts have a visibly prioritized 3D viewport and uncluttered controls; the landing view is comprehensible without a wall of text.
- [ ] Gene Light still renders both side-by-side references with synchronized orbit/zoom, front/side/back presets, Toon/PBR switch and outlines on/off; both backgrounds remain light gray. Creator/asset attribution and full notices remain discoverable.
- [ ] Synthetic rigs retain working BDEF/SDEF/QDEF, poses, motions, seek/playback, supported morph controls, IK/append, physics, local-file/binding workflows and exports (with sensible conditional control visibility). All formerly reachable **supported** Demo actions remain reachable from the unified page.
- [ ] Relevant browser tests are updated to enter the unified UI and interact with it end to end, including model switching **both directions**, feature controls, resize/mobile layout, error/recovery, resource cleanup, and no console/shader/network failures. Existing independent numerical/conformance tests continue to run without altered expected behavior.
- [ ] Inspect actual browser screenshots for the landing view, a representative motion/morph/IK/physics rig and a narrow viewport. Specifically evaluate viewport prominence, unnecessary copy, controls' legibility, and availability of key features. Record evidence/findings; do not substitute a DOM-only test for a visual check.
- [ ] Run applicable `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run check:links`, and `git diff --check`; document actual outcomes, justified skips, and any environment constraints. Keep `README`/demo usage and relevant test URLs in sync.
- [ ] Keep implementation scoped to unified public-demo layout and integration, necessary tests/docs, and directly related lifecycle fixes. No new independent rendering/physics requirements or speculative framework.

## Optional validation

Native WebGPU smoke test if a GPU adapter exists; otherwise note the skip (WebGL2 remains the required browser path).

## Required post-merge verification

After the merge-triggered GitHub Pages deployment, open https://takahirox.github.io/mmd-gltf/ and verify the **single-page** Gene/rig selection, representative playback/morph and physics controls, the comparison toggles, credit/notices and desktop/mobile presentation, without runtime or asset errors. Record the published commit and Pages workflow outcome. Publication-only checks are **post-merge**, not pre-merge blockers.
